name: Steam Frame controllers
source: Read from SteamVR's drivers/frame_controller/resources/input/frame_controller_profile.json on the Fedora test laptop, 2026-11-17 (binding-image points and order dropped).

/input/grip.note: analog: set click thresholds for grab actions

notes: Not a Touch layout: left has a D-pad, View and a bumper; right has A, B, X and Y, Menu and a bumper.
Steam Input must be off for the game (Properties > Controller > Disable Steam Input) on the machine that runs it, or SteamVR never gives the game input focus (IsInputAvailable stays false).
SteamVR falls back to a Frame binding, then OpenXR generic, then Oculus Touch remapped; with only Touch bindings B/Y land on odd buttons.
The HMD's type is frame_hmd; '(frame_hmd) has no configured binding' in logs is harmless.

linux.what: Native Steam, not Flatpak (Flatpak never sets up the wireless adapter)
linux.check: flatpak list 2>/dev/null | grep -q com.valvesoftware.Steam && echo flatpak || echo native
linux.fix: Install Steam from your distro (Fedora: RPM Fusion 'steam'), sign in, remove the Flatpak

linux.check: if command -v vainfo >/dev/null; then vainfo 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'VAProfileHEVCMain.*EncSlice' && echo yes || echo no; elif command -v rpm >/dev/null; then rpm -q mesa-va-drivers-freeworld mesa-vulkan-drivers-freeworld >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo yes || echo no; else echo unknown; fi
linux.fix: Fedora: sudo dnf swap mesa-va-drivers mesa-va-drivers-freeworld && sudo dnf swap mesa-vulkan-drivers mesa-vulkan-drivers-freeworld (RPM Fusion)

linux.what: Frame wireless adapter managed by NetworkManager
linux.check: nmcli -t -f NAME connection show 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'Steam Frame' || true
linux.fix: Plug in the adapter with Steam running; keep the device managed (don't mark it unmanaged)
